Shoulder and arm trauma foundations: 2

A patient with a midshaft humeral injury cannot extend the wrist or finger metacarpophalangeal joints. Sensation is reduced in the dorsal first web space. Which nerve is most likely affected by the fracture?

  1. Ulnar nerve
  2. Median nerve
  3. Musculocutaneous nerve
  4. Radial nerve
  5. Axillary nerve
Answer and explanation

Radial nerve

The radial nerve supplies wrist and finger extensors; humeral shaft injury can cause wrist drop and dorsal first-web-space sensory loss.

Option explanations

Radial nerve: The radial nerve supplies wrist and finger extensors; humeral shaft injury can cause wrist drop and dorsal first-web-space sensory loss.

Axillary nerve: The axillary nerve supplies deltoid and sensation over the lateral shoulder; it is vulnerable with shoulder dislocation or proximal humeral injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Ulnar nerve: The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle and supplies interossei and sensation to the little finger. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Median nerve: Median nerve injury can impair thumb opposition and sensation in the radial palmar digits. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Musculocutaneous nerve: This nerve supplies major elbow flexors and sensation over the lateral forearm. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
